entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items relevant to the River Brain, all from within approximately the last 30 days or otherwise newly surfaced in 2026:

---

- **New book published, Jan. 13, 2026:** 
*The Historical Archaeology of Michigan* by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski was published by University Press of Florida on January 13, 2026 (280 pages).
 
The book covers the past 400 years of Michigan history through archaeological themes of entrepreneurship, immigration, capitalism, and civil rights, including chapters on European colonization, the fur trade, and 19th-century logging.
 (JSTOR / University Press of Florida)

- **Federal recognition bill reintroduced in House, May 8, 2025, Senate companion June 26, 2025:** 
U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) reintroduced the bipartisan Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act alongside Rep. John James (R-MI-10) on May 8, 2025.
 
Senators Elissa Slotkin and Gary Peters introduced companion Senate legislation on June 26, 2025.
 
The Grand River Bands are described as the last treaty tribe east of the Mississippi River without federal recognition.
 (Scholten House press release / Slotkin Senate press release)

- **H.R. 3255 in active 119th Congress:** 
The Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025 (H.R. 3255) formally affirms federal recognition of the tribe and makes members eligible for services and benefits provided to federally recognized tribes, regardless of reservation status.
 
The designated service area spans Newaygo, Oceana, Kent, Muskegon, and Ottawa Counties in Michigan.
 (Congress.gov)

- **GRPM "Ice Age: Michigan's Frozen Secrets" exhibit, open as of July 2026:** 
*Ice Age: Michigan's Frozen Secrets* and *Snow: Tiny Crystals, Global Impact* are now open at the Grand Rapids Public Museum.
 
The Ice Age exhibit explores North America during the last glacial period, featuring real Ice Age fossils including bones from the recently discovered "Clapp Family Mastodon."
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

- **GRPM Anishinaabe Star Knowledge planetarium show, active summer 2026:** 
The GRPM is currently featuring planetarium shows including *Anishinaabe Star Knowledge*, alongside *Secrets of the Sun* and *Dinosaurs: A Story of Survival*.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items for the River Brain, all from approximately the last 30 days or items not yet captured as of August 1, 2026:

---

- 
**Michigan Transformational Brownfield Program reformed, July 22, 2026:** Gov. Whitmer signed SB 723 into law as Public Act 36 of 2026, revising the state's Transformational Brownfield Program by expanding oversight, increasing transparency, and tying state tax reimbursements to measurable project performance.
 
The law doubles the post-construction tax capture cap from $1.6 billion to $3.2 billion, taking effect immediately.
 
State officials cited stalled riverfront work in Grand Rapids as a key example of the capacity constraints the law is meant to relieve.
 (July 22, 2026, Environment+Energy Leader / Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**Fulton & Market towers incentive capacity unlocked, mid-July 2026:** Major waterfront developments in Grand Rapids, Muskegon, and Holland are expected to benefit from the expanded Transformational Brownfield Program.
 
The Grand Rapids riverfront towers had stalled as state incentives ran dry, with developers saying progress depended on lawmakers restoring key state incentives.
 (July 14–22, 2026, Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**Former Naval Reserve Center riverfront site auctioned, May 20, 2026:** The GSA formally listed the former Navy and Marine Corps Reserve Center in Grand Rapids for public purchase; the nearly 3.47-acre parcel contains four buildings totaling 48,120 square feet.
 
GSA Administrator Edward Forst stated the sale "will save taxpayers nearly $350,000 in annual operating costs and $27 million in cost avoidance."
 (May 20, 2026, GSA.gov)

- 
**Parks department acquires 6 land-bank lots for trails and green space, May 2026:** The Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation Department acquired six lots from the land bank, deemed unbuildable for housing, and is making plans for trails and green space as part of its network.
 (May 11, 2026, Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**New brownfield hearings scheduled for July 21, 2026:** Grand Rapids officials considered tax incentives for two projects, including a nearly 100,000-square-foot industrial facility; both had received preliminary approval from the Brownfield Redevelopment Authority, with public hearings scheduled for July 21.
 
Profile Films sought a brownfield plan amendment to be reimbursed for about $5 million in eligible activities, plus an industrial development district designation and a 12-year industrial facilities exemption certificate.
 (June 19 / July 2026, WOOD TV / Yahoo News)

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found within approximately the last 30 days (relative to August 2, 2026):

---

- 
**Grand River dam removal construction began July 1, 2026:** After 18 years of planning, in-river construction commenced on July 1 to remove four low-head dams from downtown Grand Rapids. The July 1 start date aligns with state regulatory requirements protecting fish spawning periods and preventing sea lamprey movement past the Sixth Street Dam.
 (City of Grand Rapids / Spectrum News)

- 
**Two-year construction timeline confirmed:** Over the next two years, the four lower-reach dams will be removed and replaced with boulder arch structures, constructed riffles, and scattered habitat boulders. Construction is expected to be completed by end of 2027, weather and river conditions permitting.
 (WWMT / City of Grand Rapids)

- 
**Contractor and first work scope identified:** The Taplin Group is the city's contractor for the lower-reach project and is building causeways in the coming weeks to allow construction equipment to travel safely in the river, plus a cofferdam to isolate a section of Dam 2 for the boulder arch feature.
 (City of Grand Rapids)

- 
**MDHHS 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guides released June 8, 2026:** MDHHS published updated consumption guidelines covering 696 Michigan waterbodies, including Southwest Michigan waters covering the Grand River corridor. Statewide, 59 guidelines were relaxed and 65 became more protective compared to prior year.
 (MDHHS / WNEM)

- 
**Federal USDA funding of $11,026,695 confirmed March 23, 2026** for the lower Grand River restoration covering an approximately 2,887-foot stretch through downtown Grand Rapids, channeled through the USDA to improve public safety, restore aquatic habitat for native Great Lakes fish and mussel species, and enhance river access.
 (Rep. Hillary Scholten press release)

No new Grand River-specific EGLE permit actions or public health (E. coli/contact) advisories for the Grand River in Kent County were found within the last 30 days. The most recent public health advisory on record for this stretch remains prior to August 2026.

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since approximately July 2, 2026):

---

- **In-river dam removal construction started July 1, 2026:** 
After 18 years of planning, crews entered the water on July 1 to begin removing four low-head dams from downtown, a date aligned with state regulatory requirements protecting fish spawning periods.
 
The lower reach is expected to be completed by end of 2027; the first near-term task is installing scour protection around Gillett Bridge piers before placing a cofferdam to isolate a section for construction of the first boulder arch structure.
 (July 1, 2026, Spectrum News / WOODTV)

- **Return to the River Festival 2026 dates set, Aug 22-23:** 
DGRI's Instagram confirmed the festival is scheduled for August 22 and 23, 2026, as a free music and art festival in downtown Grand Rapids.
 
The festival will span three Riverwalk locations: 555 Monroe, Sixth Street Park, and Canal Park in downtown Grand Rapids, all connected and within walking distance.
 (DGRI Instagram, circa July 2026)

- **Grand River Edges' Trail extension groundbreaking, June 15, 2026:** 
Construction started on a new Greenway extension between Leonard Street NW and Ann Street NW near downtown Grand Rapids; the segment, called the Grand River Edges' Trail, will be three-quarters of a mile long and will eventually include street crossings, lighting, benches, and native plants.
 
The trail extension is expected to be complete by the end of 2026.
 (WOODTV, June 15, 2026)

- **GRPM Grand River Adventure event announced for Aug 15, 2026:** 
The Grand Rapids Public Museum announced its 4th annual Grand River Adventure for August 15, 2026, celebrating the history, science, culture, art, and stewardship of the Grand River Watershed.
 
The one-day, open-house style event invites families and community members on an immersive journey through the river's past, present, and future, with a focus on watershed preservation.
 (GRPM website, current listing)

- **Upper Reach EIS public comment closed May 22, 2026:** 
The Environmental Impact Study process for the Upper Reach (Sixth Street Dam) is currently underway; the public comment period closed May 22, 2026, and a construction timeline will not be available until the EIS process is complete and a permittable design is finalized.
 (Grand Rapids Whitewater, updated June 2026)

- **Grand River gage height very low as of Aug 1, 2026:** 
USGS monitoring recorded a gage height of 1.16 ft at the Grand River at Grand Rapids as of August 1, 2026 at 8:00 PM EDT, provisional data.
 This is notably low and relevant to in-river construction conditions. (USGS Water Data, Aug 1, 2026)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (and the most recent weeks of the broader July 2026 window), relevant to the Grand River Brain reference model:

---

- **Dam removal and habitat construction underway, July 1, 2026:** 
After 18 years of planning, in-river construction began July 1, 2026, with crews removing four low-head dams from downtown Grand Rapids. The July 1 start date was set by state regulatory requirements to protect fish spawning periods and prevent invasive sea lamprey from moving past the Sixth Street Dam.
 (Spectrum Local News / City of Grand Rapids)

- **Sea lamprey barrier EIS process active, Sixth Street Dam design timeline set:** 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers officially resumed the Upper Reach Environmental Impact Statement process in spring 2026. A public scoping meeting was held April 22, 2026, with a 30-day comment period closing May 22, 2026. A draft EIS is anticipated in July 2027.
 Separately, 
GLFC aquatic connectivity coordinator Lisa Walter stated: "We're looking at probably 2028 until we have a project design selected."
 (Bridge Michigan / Grand Rapids Whitewater)

- **Snuffbox mussel relocation completed prior to construction:** 
Relocation of threatened and endangered mussel species, including snuffbox, was required and completed prior to the July 1 in-river construction start. The project design reduced impacts to endangered mussels to the greatest extent possible, and pre-construction relocation was determined to have the most ecological benefit for these species.
 (Grand Rapids Whitewater)

- **Lake sturgeon research funding for 2026 shifted to Great Lakes Fishery Trust:** 
Funding for Grand River lake sturgeon research in 2026 is provided by the Great Lakes Fishery Trust
, a change from prior U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service GLFWRA grants. (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

- **New Michigan state-record gizzard shad caught in Grand River, April 22, 2026:** 
Sedrick Neinhuis was fishing on the Grand River on April 22, 2026, and landed a new state-record gizzard shad weighing 4.45 pounds and measuring 20.3 inches, surpassing the previous record of 4.12 pounds set on Lake St. Clair in 1996.
 (Michigan DNR / WGRD)

- **Six invasive plant species added to Michigan's prohibited/restricted lists, effective June 19, 2026:** 
The Michigan Commission of Agriculture and Rural Development voted on May 20, 2026, to add callery pear, common buckthorn, glossy buckthorn, Japanese barberry, water hyacinth, and water lettuce to Michigan's prohibited and restricted plant lists.
 Several of these (water hyacinth, water lettuce) are aquatic and relevant to Grand River watershed monitoring. (Michigan Invasive Species Program)

entries.title: Hydrology and weather
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (since ~July 3, 2026). Note that the major spring flood event (April 2026) is already prior documented history for the River Brain; only items below are newly surfaced or represent a change in status.

---

- **No active flood watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect at the Grand River at Grand Rapids gauge (GDRM4) as of July 28, 2026**, the most recent NWS update. 
The NOAA gauge page shows no watches, warnings, or advisories in effect, last updated July 28, 2026.


- **Michigan drought conditions have eased substantially by late July 2026.** 
As of July 21, 2026, only about 2% of Michigan (approximately 1,479 square miles) is under active drought, with 0.8% (742 sq mi) in moderate drought (D1) and 0.8% (737 sq mi) in severe drought (D2).
 This is a sharp improvement from the 34%+ drought coverage documented in fall 2025.

- **River flow at Grand Rapids is running well below seasonal normal in early July 2026.** 
The gauge at Grand Rapids was flowing at approximately 2,280 cfs at 2.15 ft, down 9% day-over-day, with a 10-day average of 2,841 cfs peaking at 3,180 cfs, and forecast to recede to roughly 2,092 cfs by July 6, running well below seasonal normal.
 (Note: this snapshot appears to be from early July 2026 per the Snoflo forecast date.)

- **Grand Rapids precipitation is running 2.05 inches below normal for July 2026 month-to-date as of August 1.** 
NWS climate data shows July month-to-date precipitation at 1.81 inches versus a normal of 3.86 inches, a deficit of 2.05 inches, while year-to-date precipitation of 24.10 inches is 1.28 inches above the annual normal of 22.82 inches.


- **A separate July 2026 Michigan flood emergency does not affect the Grand River basin directly.** 
On July 9, 2026, Governor Whitmer declared a state of emergency for Antrim, Cheboygan, and Emmet counties following an intense rainstorm on June 29, 2026, which severely damaged roads and infrastructure
, all of which are in northern Michigan well outside the Grand River watershed.

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me check for any very recent updates from the past ~30 days (July 2026 onward) specifically:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (July 1, 2026 to August 2, 2026):

---

- **Lower Reach in-river construction started July 1, 2026**, the regulatory-earliest date allowed under state permit to protect fish spawning and maintain sea lamprey blockage at Sixth Street Dam. Contractor Taplin Group entered the river and began installing turbidity curtains. (City of Grand Rapids press release, Spectrum News, July 1-2 2026)

- 
Over the weeks following July 1, Taplin Group began building river causeways for equipment access, and a cofferdam is being constructed to isolate a section of Dam 2 for the boulder arch feature.
 (City of Grand Rapids PublicInput page, updated ~July 2026)

- 
Ah-Nab-Awen Park remains fully closed through the project period; Gillett Bridge remains open.
 
The park closure also forced the July 4 fireworks launch to move from the Gillett Bridge to Fulton Street Bridge.
 (City of Grand Rapids PublicInput, WOODTV, July 1 2026)

- 
The active construction season is expected to run roughly July through mid-October or early November each year, weather and river conditions permitting.
 
Season 2 is anticipated for summer 2027 and will involve removal of the remaining low-head dams.
 (Spectrum News July 2, 2026; City PublicInput ~July 2026)

- **Sixth Street Dam Upper Reach EIS:** 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers officially resumed the EIS process in spring 2026; a public scoping meeting was held April 22 and the 30-day comment period closed May 22, 2026. A draft EIS is now anticipated in July 2027.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater project page, updated June 1 2026)

- 
Details and timelines for the Upper Reach (Ann Street to Bridge Street), which may include removing the Sixth Street Dam and constructing a new sea lamprey barrier, are still to come.
 
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has set a target of completing a draft EIS by approximately June 2027.
 (ExperienceGR, WZZM13, updated ~July 2026 and April 2026)

---

No substantive new Lower Reach construction milestones or Upper Reach EIS updates have been published since July 2, 2026. The most recent confirmed River Brain update point is the July 1 construction start and the associated Ah-Nab-Awen Park and fireworks logistics changes.
